title: Keeping up with Armstrong, Hines and Henderson; teamwork
summary: He says his band was first in the East, and that Fletcher Henderson sacrificed teamwork for sensation.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I meant musically. Were you keeping up with the development in music?

Oh, yes. We used to hear over [there] from people coming backward and forward, and getting letters from home. And all like that. What was going on. We saw the rise of Louis Armstrong and Earl Hines, you know what I mean? And heard his first number on scat singing, you know? (sings) And he'd say, instead of saying, (unintelligible). And we knew that the Savoy was going and what Chick Webb was doing a good job and all like that. But, still, they had to catch us. Because when we left there, we were the first.
In the East. I don't know what was

happening out West, but we were the first because the man that could have been first, he wasn't. That was because he sacrificed for sensation, he sacrificed teamwork. That was Fletcher Henderson. And, but you can't do that. That's the reason as a good football player, having been the coach of a football team, Notre Dame. Reason they were the greatest. It was because of the teamwork. And when the leader of an organization forgets that teamwork, the individuals don't matter. It's the teamwork. And that's why we were so far ahead of them. And Duke wasn't, there wasn't no Duke then.
